quarantined_leads.lead: The New York Times reported that federal prosecutors in Minnesota had been preparing possible civil-rights and false-statement charges against ICE deportation officer Christian Castro over the January shooting of Julio C. Sosa-Celis, but that the plan fell apart before Castro was released from Texas custody. The report also said DHS disclosed that Castro was suspended without pay while the federal investigation continued.
quarantined_leads.source_title: An ICE Shooting, an Extradition Showdown and the Federal Case That Stalled
quarantined_leads.subject_response: The New York Times reported that attempts to reach Castro for comment while he was jailed and after release were unsuccessful. A DOJ official said prosecutors had not reached a conclusion and would not rush the investigative process; the U.S. Attorney's Office for Minnesota declined comment.
quarantined_leads.reason: The current-window report concerns a named ICE employee with an explicit Trump-administration federal law-enforcement role, but no federal civil-rights or false-statement charge was filed. The possible-charge account relies on statements from two attorneys and an anonymous source, no official federal charging or disciplinary record was retrieved, and no direct subject response was obtained. The report is retained as a lead only and is not converted into a criminal-charge or misconduct event. The related Minnesota state charges and prior federal extradition ruling were outside this window or already covered by another agent and were not duplicated.

handoffs: A01-Federal-Executive-Watch handoff concerning the Christian Castro report was reviewed. No return handoff was required; the lead remains quarantined pending an official federal action or stronger evidence.
